text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 0.75% today, capping a strong two-week rally of 8.07%. The immediate driver appears to be easing geopolitical oil supply concerns: Saudi Arabia announced ship-to-ship crude transfers to replace pipeline damage, which calmed fears of export disruptions and sent oil prices lower globally (Brent crude at $130.80/barrel). For a refiner, lower crude costs typically improve margins—the spread between what they pay for oil and what they sell refined products for widens. Meanwhile, U.S. refineries are running at 96.8% capacity, close to full utilization, which means the company can process more barrels at better margins.

The broader backdrop supporting this two-week move is the retreat of acute Middle East supply shocks. Signals that the U.S. may be nearing an end to its Iran conflict, combined with Saudi Arabia's quick action to stabilize oil flows after pipeline damage, have reduced the tail-risk premium that was pushing crude prices higher earlier in September. For a refiner, a stable or declining crude price environment—especially when demand remains steady—is favorable territory.
